_comment: Every router mount / route that is INTENTIONALLY reachable without
authentication. AGENTS.md: "New public routes outside this list are P0."
surface from server/index.js and fails on any difference, in either
direction. To add a legitimate public route: get owner review, then add it
here with a reason. Identity is router file + mount path (never line
numbers); route entries are METHOD + full path as the scanner prints them
A '[conditional: <predicate>]' suffix is part of the identity: the
registration sits inside an if/loop/function, and the suffix carries the
enclosing predicate chain. Moving it to unconditional top level OR
changing the predicate (=== flipped to !==) changes the key and forces

mounts.reason: Pre-router middleware inventoried as USE surface: the global helmet CSP selector (embed vs strict headers, always next()s), embed-CORS + privacy header stamps (pest-forecast, secure-card), and unobservable-when-dark 404 gates (payer statements, lawn assessment, careers, pest identifier, AI content report, public MCP/A2A, ops-digest ingest while OPS_DIGEST_INGEST_TOKEN is unset) — each either sets headers and next()s or 404s while its GATE_* is off. Also the consultation page's pre-parser guard (/api/public/inspection): 404s while GATE_LEAD_INSPECTION_LINK is dark or the token is not validly signed (live for non-GET), before the limiter and body parsers. The appointment and re-service pre-limiter guards likewise return only a generic 404 while their gates are dark, before shared rate limiting and body parsing. The visitPrepPreParserGuard entry is the visit-prep photos sub-gate + token-shape check (GATE_VISIT_PREP_PHOTOS) mounted ahead of the shared body parsers so a dark or malformed photos request 404s before any parse (always next() or 404). The mapImagePreGuard entry is the estimate map-image proxy's pre-limiter guard (GET/HEAD /api/estimates/:token/map/(satellite|overlay) only, case-insensitive): it stamps no-store/CORP/no-referrer headers and answers the generic 404 for the overlay while GATE_ESTIMATE_SHOW_YOUR_WORK is dark, before the global limiter (always next() or 404).

Anonymous, cookie-free blog read-depth beacon (owner-approved 2026-09-27, "E2: cookie-free read-depth counts") — dark behind GATE_BLOG_READ_DEPTH (generic unknown-route 404 while off, before the limiter below, house dark-GATE_* contract), its own 120 req/min per-IP rate limiter applied after the gate check, no-store/noindex privacy headers stamped first, and a 1 KB capped express.text() body parse. Mounted above the global cors() (a dark OPTIONS preflight gets the same 404), the global /api/ limiter and the body parsers, and ends in a terminal generic 404 so nothing falls through to the request logger. Site is derived ONLY from the Origin header against the fixed spoke-fleet registry (never the body); a missing/null/unknown origin drops the beacon with 204 and no write. A beacon counts only for a path the claimed site's own sitemap-index.xml (else sitemap.xml) lists (cached 6 h per site), and each (day, site, path, milestone) bucket stops at 2,000 a day. No per-source state beyond the one-minute per-IP limiter. Stores only an aggregate daily count (day/site/path/milestone); no cookie, user agent or referrer is read, and nothing per-visitor is stored or logged. See docs/public-route-contracts.md.

Signed satellite image proxy: the lead-form lookup, customer service report and portal station map carry short-lived HMAC-signed paths (services/signed-map-image.js, key derived from REPORT_PIN_SECRET||JWT_SECRET, 2 h expiry; 24 h for the lead-form lookup) instead of Google Static Maps URLs that embedded the server Maps key. The route reads ONLY the signed token in the path — never a query param — rebuilds the keyless Static Maps URL from the signed, range-checked lat/lng/zoom/size/scale/maptype, appends the key inside the fetch and streams the bytes, so it cannot become an open proxy or SSRF. Every refusal (bad shape/signature, expired, no key, upstream failure) answers one generic 404 with no-store/no-referrer/CORP cross-origin; its own 60 req/min per-IP (IPv6 /64) limiter (429 stamped with the same headers) fronts the mount, which is mounted in server/index.js above the global cors(), the global limiter and the body parsers (so an OPTIONS preflight also gets the router's generic 404, not cors()'s 204); no server-side image cache. The router stamps the privacy headers and applies the limiter to EVERY request under the mount (any method/subpath, case-insensitive, trailing slash) and ends in a terminal catch-all that answers the same generic 404 for anything but a valid GET/HEAD /:token (the inline USE entries — header stamp, terminal 404, and a last error handler that turns any error, e.g. a malformed percent-encoding, into that same 404 — and the limiter USE entry). See docs/public-route-contracts.md.
Stripe webhook — signature-verified in-handler (stripe.webhooks.constructEvent over the raw body; rejects when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset)
SendGrid event webhook — ECDSA signature over the raw body verified in-handler (x-twilio-email-event-webhook-signature)
Resend event webhook — Svix HMAC signature verified in-handler with a 5-minute replay window (RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET; fails closed when unset)
